title: PB 330 rubber (NSIC Rb 06): Characteristics
metaDescription: PB 330 rubber is a rubber variety from Prang Besar. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: PB 330 is a registered rubber variety, also sold or known as NSIC Rb 06. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2001 as NSIC 2001 Rb 06. Prang Besar bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where PB 330 rubber is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Rb 06, this is the same rubber. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [rubber variety finder](/crop-varieties/rubber), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit rubber fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 2,380 to 2,780 kg/ha/yr on virgin bark, 2,820 on renewed bark.
**Fruit:** Pale yellow latex, dry rubber content about 40.8 percent.
Moderate Oidium and Colletotrichum, about 4 percent brown bast.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: highest dry rubber content in the NSIC rubber list (about 40.8 percent). Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant PB 330 rubber

Rubber clones differ in latex yield and in how they take tapping and wind. Plant budded clones from an accredited nursery. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Rb 06 the same as PB 330?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Rb 06 is another name for PB 330, registered as NSIC 2001 Rb 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of PB 330?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
